x.ASV: that sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus upon the waters, saying, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people terrible from their beginning onward, a nation that meteth out and treadeth down, whose land the rivers divide!
x.Darby: that sendest ambassadors over the sea, and in vessels of papyrus upon the waters, [saying,] Go, swift messengers, to a nation scattered and ravaged, to a people terrible from their existence and thenceforth; to a nation of continued waiting and of treading down, whose land the rivers have spoiled!

x.YLT: That is sending by sea ambassadors, Even with implements of reed on the face of the waters, --Go, ye light messengers, Unto a nation drawn out and peeled, Unto a people fearful from its beginning and onwards, A nation meeting out by line, and treading down, Whose land floods have spoiled.

nt: The phrase **the one sending envoys** refers to the nation of Cush. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that land sending envoys]

Isaiah is using **on the face of the waters** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the surface of the waters.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [on the surface of the waters]

The words **heightened** and **shaved** are a passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use these forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a nation whose people are tall and shave their skin] or [a nation whose people are tall and have smooth skin]

The expression **feared** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a people whom all nations fear]

The expressions **line, line** and **trampling** together express a single idea. The expression **line, line**, which refers to the boundaries around nations, tells what characterizes the **trampling**, that is, the conquests, of the people of Cush. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [a nation that conquers other countries and takes their territories]

The phrase “line, line” could refer to: (1) territories that the people of Cush conquer (the ULT follows that interpretation) or (2) the foreign language of the people of Cush. Alternate translation: [a nation of strange speech] or (3) the military strength of the nation of Cush. Alternate translation: [a strong nation]

x.ASV: All ye inhabitants of the world, and ye dwellers on the earth, when an ensign is lifted up on the mountains, see ye; and when the trumpet is blown, hear ye.
x.Darby: All ye inhabitants of the world, and dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, see ye, and when a trumpet is blown, hear ye!
x.KJV: All ye inhabitants of the world, and dwellers on the earth, see ye, when he lifteth up an ensign on the mountains; and when he bloweth a trumpet, hear ye.
x.YLT: All ye inhabitants of the world, And ye dwellers of earth, At the lifting up of an ensign on hills ye look, And at the blowing of a trumpet ye hear.

nt: The terms **dwellers of the world** and **inhabitants of the earth** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Every one of you who lives on the earth]

Isaiah is using **when a banner is lifted up on the mountains** to describe something that was ongoing. This provides the background for the command **may you see** that follows. Connect this clause to the verse in a way that makes it clear in your language that this clause is describing something that was ongoing in the background. Alternate translation: [All dwellers of the world and inhabitants of the earth, while a banner is being lifted up on the mountains, may you see, and while a shofar is being blown, may you hear]

The expression **is lifted up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when someone lifts up a banner]

Isaiah is saying what he wants his audience to do. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [I desire that you see] or [they should see]

The expression **is blown** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and when someone blows a shofar]

Isaiah is saying what he wants his audience to do. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [I desire that you hear] or [they should hear]

x.ASV: For thus hath Jehovah said unto me, I will be still, and I will behold in my dwelling-place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
x.Darby: For thus hath Jehovah said unto me: I will take my rest, and I will observe from my dwelling-place like clear heat upon herbs, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
x.KJV: For so the Lord said unto me, I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place like a clear heat upon herbs, and like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
x.YLT: For thus said Jehovah unto me, `I rest, and I look on My settled place, As a clear heat on an herb. As a thick cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

nt: The point of this comparison is that just as **heat glowing because of light** is present yet calm, so Yahweh is watching quietly from his dwelling. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like the quiet presence of heat shimmering in sunlight]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest** forms quietly, so Yahweh is watching calmly from his dwelling. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like dew clouds that form silently in the summer heat]

x.KJV: For afore the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away and cut down the branches.

nt: Isaiah is using the expression **to the face of** to mean “before” or “previous to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before the harvest]

Isaiah is speaking as if God’s judgment on a nation were the **pruning** of a vine. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then he will cut down the enemy people, and their leaders he will remove, he will cut them off]
וְ⁠כָרַ֤ת הַ⁠זַּלְזַלִּים֙ בַּ⁠מַּזְמֵר֔וֹת וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠נְּטִישׁ֖וֹת הֵסִ֥יר הֵתַֽז

Here, Isaiah is using the pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then Yahweh will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks, and the spreading branches, Yahweh will remove, Yahweh will cut off]
כִּֽי־לִ⁠פְנֵ֤י קָצִיר֙ כְּ⁠תָם־פֶּ֔רַח וּ⁠בֹ֥סֶר גֹּמֵ֖ל יִֽהְיֶ֣ה נִצָּ֑ה וְ⁠כָרַ֤ת הַ⁠זַּלְזַלִּים֙ בַּ⁠מַּזְמֵר֔וֹת וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠נְּטִישׁ֖וֹת הֵסִ֥יר הֵתַֽז

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [The reason is that before harvest time, when the blossom is complete and the grape is ripening {in} the flower, then he will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks, and the spreading branches, he will remove, he will cut off.]

Isaiah is speaking as if the slain enemies were cut vegetation **left together for the bird of the mountains and for the beast of the earth**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will be left as food for the birds of the mountains and for the beasts of the earth]

The expression **will be left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [He will leave them together]

The pronoun **They** refers to the shoots and branches that Yahweh cut off in the previous verse, but those images represent the enemy army. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The dead bodies of the enemy will be left together]

Alternate translation: [And the bird will feed on them, and every beast of the earth will feed on them, throughout the entire year]

Isaiah says **every beast of the earth** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [many of the beasts of the earth]
